title: Every Active Instance publishes whether its risk capital figure rests on a finished model, and all of Keel's read Pending
content:
A.6.1.1.3.2.6.1.3 defines a status field carried by every Active Instance: it "defines whether the Instance Financial RRC is calculated based on a fully implemented risk model... or a pending risk model. If the Instance Financial RRC is calculated based on a fully implemented risk model the status is `Covered`. If... a pending risk model the status is `Pending`."

Every Kamino Instance in this chunk — USDS, USDC, USDT, USDG — carries **`Pending`** (A.6.1.1.3.2.6.1.3.1.1.1.1, …2.1, …3.1, …4.1).

Publishing model maturity as a first-class field is an unusual and valuable move. Risk capital requirements are computed from models, and a model that is not yet fully implemented produces a number whose reliability differs from one that is — a distinction normally buried in methodology appendices, if disclosed at all. Here it sits at the top of each Instance's configuration, where anyone assessing Keel's capital adequacy sees it before the parameters.

The substantive reading is more sobering than the transparency is admirable: Keel's entire live allocation book is currently capitalized against pending models. The 90% Encumbrance Ratio covenant and the Risk Capital rules that the Freezer enforces are all computed on inputs the Atlas itself flags as provisional.

The honest framing is that the Artifact tells you exactly how much to trust its own risk numbers, and the answer today is: less than it intends to eventually.
description: The RRC Framework Full Implementation Coverage status is Covered when Instance Financial RRC uses a fully implemented risk model and Pending when it does not; each Kamino Instance is marked Pending.
